evidence_quotes.quote: Elaborar un plan de acción para la implementación de estrategias ante el desabastecimiento del sistema de saneamiento básico como factor contribuyente a las infecciones diarreicas agudas en niños menores de 5 años en Secocha, 2025.

El propósito fundamental es poner en marcha intervenciones integrales y sostenibles que respondan al déficit en el acceso a servicios de saneamiento en la comunidad de Secocha. Esta iniciativa tiene como meta principal disminuir la frecuencia de IDA en niños menores de cinco años a lo largo del año 2025.

Los programas de educación en salud y hábitos sanitarios no logran cubrir de forma efectiva a toda la comunidad, mientras que las entidades responsables de temas relacionados con agua potable, saneamiento y salud pública no operan de manera articulada por lo que se espera trabajar con los actores involucradas de la comunidad de Secocha.
Se aplicarán métodos estadísticos descriptivos mediante encuestas y entrevistas
Se espera que el 80% de los hogares en situación vulnerable accedan a servicios básicos de saneamiento adecuados.

Se sugiere que el plan de acción desarrollado sea asumido como un instrumento técnico y funcional por parte de las autoridades locales, los servicios de salud y las organizaciones comunitarias en Secocha, priorizando su ejecución de forma gradual en función del grado de vulnerabilidad de cada área.

criterion_notes.c1: Addresses household and community access to basic sanitation and safe drinking water services (water supply, excreta disposal, latrines, and sewerage) in Secocha, Camaná province, Arequipa, Peru.
criterion_notes.c2: Fails under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: the document does not examine any legal, regulatory, or administrative rule-type mechanism directly governing service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, tenure/documentation rules, tariffs/cost recovery, enforcement/disconnection, or utility regulatory structure). Instead, it formulates a public-health action plan ('Plan de acción') centered on community hygiene education workshops, household water chlorination/storage, ecological/dry latrines, and community surveillance, while citing weak institutional management, scarce public investment, and poor inter-institutional coordination only as unanalysed background causes. Under the plain literal wording of Criterion 2, it mentions institutional coordination and local government management descriptively as background/intervention context rather than empirically analysing a governance factor; even if treated as broadly touching institutional factors under the plain wording, the study still fails Criteria 3, 4, and 5 and would still be excluded.
criterion_notes.c3: Fails Criterion 3 (E05): Although the abstract ('Resumen') refers to a mixed-methods design with 120 households and stakeholder interviews, the body of this postgraduate 'Trabajo Académico' contains zero primary empirical data, zero descriptive or inferential statistics, zero survey tabulations, and zero qualitative interview or observation findings. Table 3 (PDF Page 38) states the analytical methods in the future tense ('Se aplicarán métodos estadísticos descriptivos mediante encuestas y entrevistas'), Annexes 1-5 contain only blank data-collection templates, and Chapter IV presents a proposed action schedule and projected targets rather than empirical results. Nor is it a systematic empirical synthesis.
criterion_notes.c4: No measured empirical outcomes on service access, connection, continuity, or affordability are reported. Section 3.2.4 lists planned diagnostic indicators and Section 4.5 reports only projected expectations ('Se espera que el 80% de los hogares en situación vulnerable accedan a servicios básicos de saneamiento adecuados'), alongside a primary clinical target of reducing acute diarrheal infections (IDA) in children under 5.
criterion_notes.c5: Because no primary data or empirical analyses are reported—only proposed data-collection instruments, future-tense analysis tables, narrative gap descriptions, and an unexecuted/prospective action plan—an empirical exposure-outcome evaluation cannot be identified.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish with an English abstract ('Summary' on PDF Page 14). While Spanish is not among the three languages eligible without translation under Criterion 9 (English, Portuguese, Dutch), assessment/translation from the provided Spanish full text is straightforward per Criterion 10; exclusion is based on lack of empirical evidence (E05) and lack of a rule-type legal/administrative mechanism, not language.

study_design: Public-health action plan ('Trabajo Académico' / 'Plan de acción') outlining a proposed mixed-methods participatory diagnostic and community intervention without reported empirical data
population_and_sample: Community households and children under 5 years of age in Secocha, Camaná province, Arequipa, Peru (mentions a planned/selected stratified random sample of 120 households and interviews with health personnel, local authorities, and community leaders, with no empirical sample results reported)
exposure: Proposed community sanitation and public-health action plan strategies (ecological/dry latrines, safe water storage and chlorination, hygiene education workshops, and community monitoring) addressing basic sanitation deficits
outcome: Projected targets only (no empirical outcome data reported): 40% projected reduction in acute diarrheal infections (IDA) in children under 5 and 80% projected basic sanitation coverage among vulnerable households
rationale: Excluded under E05 (No empirical evidence). This 2025 postgraduate 'Trabajo Académico' is a public-health Action Plan ('Plan de acción') proposing community hygiene promotion, dry/ecological latrine installation, and local monitoring to reduce acute diarrheal infections in children under 5 in Secocha, Peru. Despite mentioning a 120-household sample and interviews in the abstract and methods, the full text reports zero primary empirical data, zero survey statistics, and zero qualitative interview findings (Table 3 describes planned analyses in the future tense, Annexes 1-5 provide blank instruments, and Chapter IV presents implementation schedules and projected targets). Additionally, it fails Criterion 2 because it examines generic community health promotion, basic sanitation project delivery, and unanalysed institutional background rather than any rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism governing service access.
